narrative.overview:
The system is engineering exactness lit by warm light. The interlocking isotype (a white and a Precission Orange arrow locking around a warm-black dot) sets the tone: two exact geometric forms meeting cleanly, on a dark ground that is never neutral. Heavy, tightly tracked Montserrat carries the precision. Granular orange-and-peach light carries the warmth: slow radial blobs, a fixed film-grain layer, glowing accents. Emphasis never changes the typeface: one phrase per headline shifts to peach, and the headline closes on a Precission Orange full stop, a small echo of the isotype's geometry.

Density is spacious and cinematic. Sections breathe (90–160px vertical padding), headlines are large, and each section has one clear focal point. The page lives almost entirely in the warm-black world, with one deliberate inversion: the Projects section rises as a paper-colored sheet with rounded top corners, so the real product work reads as the page's centerpiece.

Motion is part of the identity (the isotype assembling on load, line-by-line headline reveals, manifesto words lighting up on scroll) but it has to stay in service of the content. The confirmed anti-reference is an **overloaded, noisy** page: so many effects running at once that the content gets lost.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-black ground (never pure #000, never cool gray) with orange and peach as the only light sources.
One typeface for every headline: the accent phrase changes tone (peach on dark, orange on paper), never family or style, and the closing period is orange.
Depth from layers of translucent dark glass, not from floating white cards.
Pills and generous radii everywhere; no sharp corners on interactive elements.
Film grain over the whole page, matching the brand piece.
One light "sheet" section (Projects) that inverts the palette for emphasis.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Every dark surface is a warm black or brown (#0E0806, #1A0D08, #3A1509, #5C2412, or cream-tinted transparency). Neutral grays and pure #000 never appear.

rules.name: The Signal-and-Glow Rule
rules.body: Orange marks action and state; peach marks accent and light. Don't use peach for a primary action, and don't use orange for body-level accents on dark surfaces.

rules.name: The Guest Color Rule
rules.body: Project, WhatsApp and error colors are guests. They appear only inside their own component and never leak into Precission's own UI.

rules.name: The One Ember Word Rule
rules.body: Each headline gets at most one accent phrase, and it usually lands at the end ("…con precisión."), followed by the orange stop. Accents change color only: no italic, no serif, no size bump. Two accents in one headline dilute both.

rules.name: The Balanced Line Rule
rules.body: Headings and eyebrows use `text-wrap: balance` and paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`, so no title or lead ends on a single orphaned word. The only deliberate single-word line is the hero's "precisión.", which is set as its own line.

rules.name: The Readable Floor Rule
rules.body: Running copy never drops below 16px (1rem), and every text role, including metadata, labels and legal notes, holds at least 4.5:1 against its surface. Hierarchy between body and metadata comes from size and tone (Text Dim vs Text Faint), never from fading text below AA. Counters use tabular numerals so they do not jitter while counting.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Montserrat at headline sizes and above always takes negative tracking (-0.02em to -0.035em) and a line-height at or below 1.05. Loose display type breaks the precision.

rules.name: The Glass-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: On dark surfaces, a container is warm-black glass with a hairline border. Opaque light cards appear only on the paper Projects sheet and as the client-logo plates.

rules.name: The Negative-Spread Rule
rules.body: Every shadow uses a negative spread about half its blur, so it pools beneath the element instead of haloing around it.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: At most five things loop on their own at any time: the two hero blobs, the two orbit rings and the client-logo marquee. Everything else moves once (entrance, reveal, the isotype assembly) or only in response to the visitor (hover, scroll-linked manifesto and steps line). Attention cues (the WhatsApp pulse, the scroll cue) play three times and stop.

dos: Do keep every dark surface warm (#0E0806 / #1A0D08 / browns); tint borders and transparencies with cream (247, 237, 230), never with white or gray.
Do give each headline at most one accent phrase in the same Montserrat, peach on dark and orange on paper, and close it with the orange stop (`.` after the ``).
Do build dark containers as translucent warm-black glass with hairline borders and 12–20px backdrop blur.
Do make interactive elements pill-shaped, with a 2–4px lift and a warm color shift on hover, eased on `cubic-bezier(.22, 1, .36, 1)`.
Do keep project, WhatsApp and error colors scoped to their own components.
Do honor `prefers-reduced-motion`: turn off drift, grain, marquee and reveal motion and show content in its final state.
donts: Don't bring back a serif or italic accent inside headlines; the user rejected it as a generic AI-landing tell. Emphasis is color plus the orange stop.
Don't let the page become overloaded or noisy. New motion or effects must not compete with the existing blobs, grain and marquee for attention, and content always wins.
Don't add infinite animations, scroll-linked scaling or pulsing glows beyond the hero; they break the Motion Budget Rule.
Don't use pure black, neutral gray or cool shadows anywhere; shadows are black or brown-tinted with a large negative spread.
Don't use peach for primary actions or orange for passive accents on dark surfaces.
Don't introduce sharp corners on interactive elements or containers.
Don't set Montserrat display sizes with positive tracking or line-height above 1.05.
